newsitem.title: JAPAN: Daihatsu to start selling new Terios next month.
newsitem.headline: Daihatsu to start selling new Terios next month.

text.p: Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it plans to start selling a new version of its Terios compact sport-utility vehicle in Japan next month and will launch exports of the model, mostly to Europe, soon after.
Daihatsu said it hoped the new Terios, a 1.3 litre-engine four-wheel-drive vehicle, would help bolster sales and offset an expected slump in car demand when Japan raises its consumption tax in April.

The car will go on sale in Japan on the day of the tax increase, April 1, with a monthly domestic sales target of 2,000, while Daihatsu plans to export half that number per month. Exports will begin in May and actual overseas sales should start from June.

"We plan to export a total of 1,000 units a month to Europe, Australia and Asia," Daihatsu president Iichi Shingu told reporters. Of the planned monthly exports, 80 percent will be to Europe, he added.
Daihatsu said the Terios was well-received when it was unveiled at the Geneva car show, which started last week.
Daihatsu is owned 33.4 percent by Toyota.

Asked why Daihatsu chose to launch the new model in April, a Daihatsu official said: "We hope the new model will help check a possible decline in domestic sales after an increase in the Japanese consumption tax."
Japan's consumption tax will be increased to five percent from three percent on April 1.
The domestic selling price for the Terios will start at 1.30 million yen.
